label: Castle
_model: Same kernel as barrow: an APPETITE and the ACCOMMODATION made for it. A castle's appetites are about holding — ground, fear, obedience, a name — and its accommodations are what a house does to keep them.

appetites.purpose: nobody would ever test the walls

appeasement.move: show it you are afraid, plainly and without shame
ask its permission before you pass, and wait for it
appeasement.why: the ground is still its own to grant

appetites.asks: "Who gave you leave to be here?"

appetites.purpose: an order would never need repeating

appeasement.move: carry out one order at once, without asking why
say the family name as though it still means something
appeasement.why: the name is spoken by someone living

accommodations.text: walled {conscript} in and did not open the gate again
bound {conscript} by an oath sworn on the name
made an example of {conscript}, and left it up
married {conscript} into the line whether they would or not
would not let {conscript} leave, and then could not

banner.label: the banner that was never struck
banner.function: the reason nobody ever came over the wall

deed.label: the deed that says whose ground this is
deed.function: the only proof the claim was ever good

seal.label: the seal that still commands the household
seal.function: the only thing the walls answer to

ring.label: the signet of the line, sized for a boy
ring.function: the last place the name is written

factions.name: the Garrison
factions.essence: still standing the watch they were set

factions.name: rival claimants
factions.essence: here for the deed and armed about it

factions.name: the Household
factions.essence: keeping a house whose lord is gone

factions.name: what came over the wall
factions.essence: neither knows nor cares whose keep this was

triggerGlossary.announced: came in by the gate, in the open, seen from the walls
triggerGlossary.seenTwice: caught by two watchposts, or by a watcher and a mirror
triggerGlossary.loud: steel on stone, a shout, a door forced
triggerGlossary.lingering: stayed in one place longer than a watch would allow
triggerGlossary.disturbed: moved something the garrison had set down

skirmish.avoid: they challenge before they strike — answer the challenge

fight.avoid: break the formation and the Nerve 3 tells

foes.name: Ogre
foes.note: one blow moves you a square

battle.harmedBy: anything — but the Ogre has 12 Grit; do not trade blows
battle.avoid: the Ogre was set to hold one doorway and will not leave it

foes.name: Wraith
foes.note: INCORPOREAL — chill touch ignores armour, drains 1 max Grit

nightmare.harmedBy: blessed, silvered or magical weapons for the Wraith ONLY; anything for the rest
nightmare.avoid: do not run this without an appeasement route open

terror.dangerLine: the keep is still frightening people, and needs to be

institution: heads on the gate spikes, replaced as they weathered
a gibbet in the courtyard, oiled and maintained
arrow-slits cut to cover every step of the approach
ritual: a drum on the wall, beaten at the same hour for a century
the watch calling a challenge to an empty road
weapons laid out for an inspection nobody attends
demand: a hall arranged so a visitor must cross it alone, and slowly
a chair set high enough that you must look up from the door
a room with one way in and no way to stand out of the light
wound: armour hacked apart from behind, and stacked neatly anyway
a wall of tally-marks, counting something that stopped being counted
a garrison that killed itself rather than open the gate
anchor: a banner that has never been struck, still on its staff
a standard rolled in oiled cloth, ready to raise
a great seal pressed into black wax, unbroken

features: a portcullis dropped from the inside, recently
siege-marks on a wall that was never actually stormed
a fire lit last week in a hearth three centuries cold
supplies stacked for a siege that never came
a door barred with furniture, from this side
boot-prints on the wall-walk that stop halfway

decisions.cue: a gate that will open for anyone who demands it loudly enough
decisions.cost: demanding it announces you to everything inside

resolve.success: you demand it with the right authority and the gate opens for you as it would for its lord
resolve.failure: your demand rings hollow and the garrison marks you as a pretender: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: go round by the sally port: two Turns, unannounced

decisions.cue: a challenge called down from the wall, and a right answer you do not know
decisions.cost: a wrong answer is taken as an assault

resolve.success: the countersign is in what you already passed — you give it and are admitted as expected
resolve.failure: you answer wrong and the watch stands to: the next area's encounter begins hostile
resolve.orElse: do not answer at all; go over the wall, one Turn and a Brawn roll

decisions.cue: a body left hanging as an example, and an obvious kindness in cutting it down
decisions.cost: the example was the point

resolve.success: you cut it down with enough ceremony that the garrison approves rather than objects
resolve.failure: you have destroyed the keep's warning and it wants a replacement: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it; nothing changes and nothing is owed

decisions.cue: a war-drum you could beat, or leave
decisions.cost: beating it calls the garrison to muster — for you or against you

resolve.success: the muster forms up and takes its orders from you for one scene
resolve.failure: the muster forms up and you are what it has come to deal with
resolve.orElse: do not beat it: the way on is longer by one Turn

decisions.cue: a room you must cross in full view of the arrow-slits
decisions.cost: being watched crossing is exactly what the room is for

resolve.success: you cross fast and low and are not fired upon
resolve.failure: you are shot at: take 2 Grit and roll the clock
resolve.orElse: walk it openly and slowly, hands visible — no harm, but you are announced

decisions.cue: a prisoner still in the oubliette, alive by some means
decisions.cost: letting them out means they know the keep and want out of it

resolve.success: they trade the garrison's watch-pattern for their freedom, and it is true
resolve.failure: they trade you a lie and go ahead of you to raise the alarm
resolve.orElse: leave them: the way on is unchanged and you will hear them for hours

situations.doing: standing a watch on a road nobody uses
situations.onArrival: they challenge you, and wait for a countersign
situations.because: the order to stand down never came
situations.offer: give them any countersign said with confidence and they pass you through

situations.doing: beating the hour on a drum with no skin left
situations.onArrival: the beat stops when you enter
situations.because: the hour must be kept or the watch cannot change
situations.offer: keep the beat yourself and the whole garrison changes shift, opening the wall-walk

situations.doing: measuring the great hall with a knotted cord
situations.onArrival: they put a hand on their sword and ask your business
situations.because: they mean to prove the keep is theirs by right of survey
situations.offer: offer to witness the survey and they will show you what they have already found

situations.doing: inspecting weapons that are all of them broken
situations.onArrival: they hand you one to examine and await your verdict
situations.because: the inspection was never concluded
situations.offer: condemn the weapons honestly and the armoury opens for you

situations.occupant: a single figure on the wall-walk
situations.doing: watching a road where something is genuinely coming
situations.onArrival: it points, and does not look at you
situations.because: it has seen the same thing arrive every night for three centuries
situations.offer: look where it points and it will tell you how long you have

situations.doing: hauling a portcullis that is already down
situations.onArrival: they make room for you at the winch
situations.because: the order was to close the gate and it has never been rescinded
situations.offer: help them and they will open it once, for you

temptations.cue: a banner-staff with the colours still on it
temptations.benefit: raise it and the Garrison treats you as its lord for a scene
temptations.standingDrawback: everything in the keep now knows exactly where you are

temptations.cue: a watchword scratched inside a helm
temptations.benefit: pass any challenge in the keep without a roll, once
temptations.standingDrawback: you are expected at the next post, and they wait

temptations.cue: a length of gibbet-chain, still warm
temptations.benefit: once, make one foe genuinely afraid — it breaks and flees
temptations.standingDrawback: whatever flees tells the rest what it saw

temptations.cue: a horn that calls the garrison to arms
temptations.benefit: sound it and three Skeletons fight for you for one scene
temptations.standingDrawback: they expect to be commanded again, and follow you

temptations.cue: the great seal, pressed and unbroken
temptations.benefit: one door in the keep opens because you carry it
temptations.standingDrawback: the seal is missed, and the household looks for who took it

holding.dangerLine: the ground is still owned, and knows you are on it

institution: boundary stones set closer together than any survey needs
a wall built through a room, sealing half of it off
fences inside the courtyard, dividing nothing from nothing
ritual: a rent-roll being read to an empty hall
a beating of the bounds, worn into the flagstones
a table where a claim was witnessed, still set for witnesses
demand: a door that will not open until someone asks for it aloud
a hall that reroutes you back to where you entered
a threshold worn on one side only, by people permitted to leave
wound: a deed torn in half, both halves kept
a wall pulled down and rebuilt three times in the same place
land salted inside the walls, so nothing else could hold it
anchor: a strongbox with one document in it
a survey chest, sealed, with the ribbons intact
a boundary stone brought indoors and kept warm

features: fresh mortar in a wall that should be three centuries old
a fence recently cut and badly mended
stakes driven into the courtyard in a line, not old
a room emptied of everything except the floorboards
chalk marks measuring out a room, still bright
a door rehung to open the other way

decisions.cue: a boundary you can step over, or ask to cross
decisions.cost: asking costs time; stepping costs standing

resolve.success: you ask properly and the ground grants it — the Garrison will not treat you as trespassers again
resolve.failure: you step over and are trespassers from here on: every encounter starts one step more hostile
resolve.orElse: go the long way round the boundary: two Turns

decisions.cue: a strongbox that will open for whoever holds the deed
decisions.cost: you do not hold the deed

resolve.success: you work out which half of the torn deed is here and open it with that
resolve.failure: the box holds and the attempt is recorded somewhere: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: break it: loud, roll the clock, and the contents are damaged

decisions.cue: a rival claimant offering to split what is inside
decisions.cost: splitting it means telling them what you know

resolve.success: you strike a deal that costs you nothing you needed
resolve.failure: they take the better half and the way you came in
resolve.orElse: refuse and go alone: nothing shared, nothing learned

decisions.cue: a wall built through the middle of a room
decisions.cost: the sealed half is where the way on is

resolve.success: you open a gap without bringing the rest down
resolve.failure: the wall comes down badly: roll the clock and lose a Turn
resolve.orElse: find the old door: one Turn of searching

decisions.cue: a rent-roll listing everyone who ever owed here, and a blank line
decisions.cost: signing it makes you a tenant, which has privileges

resolve.success: you sign in a way that grants passage but promises nothing
resolve.failure: you sign plainly and now owe rent to something that collects: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it unsigned; doors that check tenancy stay shut

decisions.cue: a room the keep keeps returning you to
decisions.cost: the loop is deliberate and will not simply be walked out of

resolve.success: you spot which door is the one that was added later
resolve.failure: you go round again: lose a Turn and roll the clock
resolve.orElse: break through a wall instead: loud, one Turn

situations.doing: reading a rent-roll aloud to nobody
situations.onArrival: it stops and asks whether you are on the list
situations.because: the roll must be read complete before any tenant may pass
situations.offer: have yourself entered on the roll and every internal door opens

situations.doing: arguing over a torn deed, half each
situations.onArrival: they both appeal to you at once
situations.because: neither half is worth anything alone
situations.offer: judge between them and the loser tells you what the winner would not

situations.doing: rebuilding the same wall it has rebuilt many times
situations.onArrival: it does not stop, and asks you to hold a stone
situations.because: the wall must stand and will not
situations.offer: tell it the wall is finished and it will down tools and answer questions

situations.doing: beating the bounds of a room, slowly, with a rod
situations.onArrival: it invites you to walk the bounds with it
situations.because: the boundary must be walked or the claim lapses
situations.offer: walk with it and the ground stops treating you as trespassers

situations.doing: measuring a courtyard that is bigger every time
situations.onArrival: it asks you to hold the other end of the cord
situations.because: the survey has never once agreed with itself
situations.offer: hold the cord and the courtyard resolves to one size, revealing a door

situations.doing: paying rent into an empty box, coin by coin
situations.onArrival: it looks up and asks whether the rent is due
situations.because: nobody ever came to collect and it dare not stop
situations.offer: accept the rent on the house's behalf and it will guide you anywhere inside

temptations.cue: half a torn deed, the upper half
temptations.benefit: doors that check ownership open for you
temptations.standingDrawback: the other half is somewhere, and someone is holding it

temptations.cue: a boundary stone small enough to carry
temptations.benefit: once, declare a space yours — nothing may enter it for a scene
temptations.standingDrawback: you cannot leave ground you have claimed without giving it up aloud

temptations.cue: a rent-roll with a blank line
temptations.benefit: write a name and that person owes the keep a favour, once
temptations.standingDrawback: your own name is entered directly beneath

temptations.cue: a ring of keys, every one of them for this house
temptations.benefit: one locked door per scene opens
temptations.standingDrawback: the household expects you to lock up behind you

temptations.cue: a surveyor's knotted cord
temptations.benefit: once, know exactly how far and which way the way on lies
temptations.standingDrawback: you cannot stop measuring; distances distract you

command.dangerLine: orders given here are still carried out, by whoever is nearest

institution: a duty roster chalked up, with today's date in a dead hand
bells numbered by room, all of them still wired
a chain of command painted on a wall, ranks in gold
ritual: a changing of the guard performed by two figures who never meet
orders read out at the same hour, to nobody
a salute held by a sentry who has not been relieved
demand: a hall where your own orders come back to you, obeyed
a chair placed so that whoever sits in it must be reported to
a room that will not let you leave until you have given an instruction
wound: orders countermanded in three hands, the last one shaking
a garrison that obeyed one order to the letter and starved doing it
anchor: a seal of office, still warm, on a table set for signing
a baton of command, laid down and not taken up
a written order with the wax unbroken

features: a duty roster amended recently, in chalk
a bell still swinging in an empty corridor
boots set out in a row, polished, for people who will not come
a door held open by a sentry who is no longer there
an order pinned to a board, the pin newer than the paper
a horse-line with the tack laid out and the horses long gone

decisions.cue: an order chalked on the wall that you could obey, ignore or amend
decisions.cost: obeying makes you household; amending makes you an officer

resolve.success: you obey exactly and are counted household — the Garrison stands down for you
resolve.failure: you obey wrongly, which is worse than refusing: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: ignore it and go round: one Turn, and they do not count you as theirs

decisions.cue: a sentry who will not stand aside without relief
decisions.cost: relieving them means taking their post

resolve.success: you take the post long enough to be relieved in turn, and pass
resolve.failure: you take the post and the relief does not come: lose a Turn and roll the clock
resolve.orElse: find another way past: two Turns

decisions.cue: a bell-board that would summon a servant to any room
decisions.cost: whatever answers has been waiting a long time to be useful

resolve.success: you ring for exactly the right room and something helpful arrives
resolve.failure: you ring the wrong room and something unhelpful arrives instead
resolve.orElse: do not ring: the way on is longer by one Turn

decisions.cue: a written order, sealed, addressed to the garrison
decisions.cost: reading it makes you responsible for it

resolve.success: you read it and learn what the garrison is still waiting to be told
resolve.failure: you break the seal clumsily; the order is void and the Garrison knows
resolve.orElse: deliver it unopened to whoever it names — one Turn, and they act on it

decisions.cue: two of the household awaiting an instruction from anyone at all
decisions.cost: giving one commits you to the consequence

resolve.success: your instruction is carried out well and they attach to you as staff
resolve.failure: your instruction is carried out to the letter, which is not what you meant: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: give none; they follow you anyway, waiting

decisions.cue: a baton of command laid across a threshold
decisions.cost: picking it up is picking up the post

resolve.success: you take it up and the keep addresses you as its officer
resolve.failure: you take it up and are held to an officer's standard you cannot meet: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: step over it; you pass, and nothing here answers to you

situations.doing: holding a salute that was never returned
situations.onArrival: it holds the salute, waiting
situations.because: the officer who should have returned it died first
situations.offer: return the salute and it stands down and speaks freely

situations.doing: reading the duty roster aloud to an empty yard
situations.onArrival: it reaches your position on the list and pauses
situations.because: the roster must be read complete or the watch cannot change
situations.offer: answer to a name on the roster and you are counted in the watch

situations.doing: carrying out an order that cancelled itself
situations.onArrival: they ask you which of two contradictory orders stands
situations.because: both were given and neither was withdrawn
situations.offer: choose one and the other stands down and serves you

situations.doing: stripping livery off a body, quickly
situations.onArrival: they freeze and put their hands where you can see them
situations.because: they worked out that the livery is what the keep obeys
situations.offer: trade for a set of livery and the Garrison will take you for household

situations.doing: ringing room by room, coming closer
situations.onArrival: the bell in this room begins
situations.because: someone rang for service and the house is obliging
situations.offer: answer the bell yourself before whatever is meant to arrives

situations.doing: waiting at a table set for the signing of an order
situations.onArrival: it turns the paper toward you and offers the pen
situations.because: the order was never signed and nothing may proceed without it
situations.offer: sign it and the whole household acts on it — read it first

temptations.cue: a baton of office, laid down
temptations.benefit: the Household obeys one order from you per scene
temptations.standingDrawback: you may not refuse an order given to you by anything of higher rank

temptations.cue: a set of household livery, clean
temptations.benefit: the Garrison takes you for staff and does not challenge you
temptations.standingDrawback: you are given errands, and they are noticed if left undone

temptations.cue: a bell-pull cut and carried
temptations.benefit: once, summon something from elsewhere in the keep to help
temptations.standingDrawback: whatever comes stays until it is dismissed by name

temptations.cue: a written order, sealed, unaddressed
temptations.benefit: fill in a name and that person must do one thing
temptations.standingDrawback: your own name is on the reverse in the same hand

temptations.cue: a sergeant's whistle
temptations.benefit: once, halt anything in the keep for a round
temptations.standingDrawback: everything in earshot looks to you for what comes next

lineage.dangerLine: the line is still being counted, and it is looking for the next name

institution: a family tree painted the length of a wall, the last branch bare
portraits in strict order of birth, ending abruptly
cradles stacked in a storeroom, all of them used
ritual: a christening bowl, filled and refilled
a naming-day feast laid out and never eaten
a bible with the births entered in five hands and the deaths in one
demand: a hall of mirrors hung at child-height
a chair sized for an heir, kept dusted
a room that shows you your own face in the family line
wound: a name scratched from the tree, and the plaster gouged through
portraits of children that stop at the same age
a marriage bed with the hangings cut to ribbons
anchor: a signet sized for a boy's hand
a cradle with the blankets still warm
a locket with two portraits and one of them scraped blank

features: a name added to the family tree in fresh paint
a cradle moved recently, and rocked
a portrait taken down and turned to the wall
a christening bowl with water in it
a marriage contract half-signed on a table
toys set out for a child who is not here

decisions.cue: a family tree with one bare branch, and a brush left out
decisions.cost: adding a name is a claim; the house takes claims seriously

resolve.success: you paint a name that satisfies the house without binding you
resolve.failure: you paint yourself in, and the house now expects an heir of you: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave the branch bare and go round: one Turn

decisions.cue: a locket with one portrait scraped away
decisions.cost: restoring it means deciding who was removed

resolve.success: you work out who it was from the portraits and the tree, and the house softens toward you
resolve.failure: you guess wrong and name the wrong person: +1 Bane, and the house is colder
resolve.orElse: leave it scraped; nothing gained, nothing owed

decisions.cue: a living claimant with a marriage contract and a pen
decisions.cost: signing gets you the run of the house as family

resolve.success: you sign in a way that grants access without obligation
resolve.failure: you have married into a line the house intends to continue
resolve.orElse: refuse: doors that check blood stay shut, one Turn to go round

decisions.cue: a cradle that rocks when nobody is near it
decisions.cost: stopping it is a kindness or an insult, depending

resolve.success: you still it gently and whatever was rocking it is grateful
resolve.failure: you still it and the house takes the loss badly: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave it rocking; you will hear it for the rest of the delve

decisions.cue: a christening bowl and a name expected of you
decisions.cost: being named into the house has privileges

resolve.success: you give a name that is accepted and are treated as kin
resolve.failure: you give your own name and the house has it now: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: decline the water; you remain a stranger and are watched as one

decisions.cue: a portrait of a child that looks unmistakably like one of you
decisions.cost: the house has noticed the resemblance too

resolve.success: you turn the resemblance to your advantage and are welcomed as returning family
resolve.failure: the house decides one of you is the heir, and will not be argued out of it
resolve.orElse: cover the portrait: one Turn, and the house resents it

situations.doing: rocking a cradle that has nothing in it
situations.onArrival: it asks you, quite reasonably, to be quiet
situations.because: the child was never brought and the rocking was never stopped
situations.offer: offer to take the watch and it will finally leave the room, and show you out

situations.doing: working on a family tree that has run out of branches
situations.onArrival: it turns and measures your face against the wall
situations.because: the line must be continued on paper if it cannot be otherwise
situations.offer: sit for it and the house treats you as kin for the rest of the delve

situations.doing: comparing signets, neither of which fits
situations.onArrival: they ask you to say which ring is the true one
situations.because: both were made and only one was worn
situations.offer: judge between them and the loser hands you what they came in with

situations.doing: filling a christening bowl that will not stay full
situations.onArrival: it holds out the ladle to you
situations.because: a naming was begun and never finished
situations.offer: finish the naming and every door that checks blood opens

situations.doing: sitting in a chair too large for it, waiting to be addressed
situations.onArrival: it looks up and asks whether you have come for it at last
situations.because: it was told to wait and nobody returned
situations.offer: tell it that it may stop waiting, and it will show you the way down

situations.doing: setting a table for a family that is not coming
situations.onArrival: she counts you and adds places
situations.because: the meal must be laid whether anyone eats or not
situations.offer: sit and eat and the household is yours for the delve

temptations.cue: a signet ring sized for a boy
temptations.benefit: doors that check blood open for you
temptations.standingDrawback: the house expects you to produce an heir, and asks

temptations.cue: a locket, one portrait scraped blank
temptations.benefit: once, be taken for someone's kin by anything here
temptations.standingDrawback: whoever was scraped out begins to be remembered as you

temptations.cue: a blanket from a cradle, warm
temptations.benefit: once, be protected as the house protects its own
temptations.standingDrawback: the house treats you as a child of it — indulged, and not consulted

temptations.cue: the register of births and deaths
temptations.benefit: write a death and the house believes it, once
temptations.standingDrawback: your own entry has been begun in the same hand

temptations.cue: a chair-back finial from an heir's seat
temptations.benefit: once, insist on precedence as family and be obeyed
temptations.standingDrawback: the rest of the line resents you, and shows it
